caption:
Curiosity did not leave you. It just got quiet.

Save this, then write down one question you have stopped asking.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#innerspeech #curiosity #aristotle #selftalk #mindset

text: “All men by nature desire to know.”
Aristotle opens his *Metaphysics* with this line.
He saw curiosity as part of being human.
You were born asking *why.*
Somewhere along the way, many of us learned to stop.
Curiosity rarely dies.
It gets quieter when we are told to just accept things.
Listen to your inner voice today.
Is it asking questions, or only repeating answers?
Try this:
Take one thing you believe.
Ask, *how do I actually know that?*
You do not need to be certain.
You only need to be willing to look.
What are you genuinely curious about that you have stopped asking?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
A curious inner voice is a thinking one.
Ask again.
*Keep the thinker curious.*

caption:
Being right is easy. Checking is the work.

Send this to someone who thinks independently.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#thinkforyourself #voltaire #criticalthinking #independentthinking #mindset

text: “It is dangerous to be right in matters on which the established authorities are wrong.”
Voltaire wrote this about the cost of independent thought.
He knew it from experience.
Authorities are not always wrong.
But they are not right just because they are authorities.
Thinking for yourself has a price.
People may disagree. Some will be annoyed.
The alternative is to borrow every conclusion.
That costs more, only later and quietly.
Try this:
Pick one view you hold because someone important holds it.
Check the reasons yourself.
You may end up agreeing.
The difference is that the view will now be yours.
Which belief of yours have you never checked for yourself?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Your own conclusions, earned slowly.
Check it yourself.
*Then it is yours.*

caption:
Happiness is not always something to add. Sometimes it is something to notice.

Save this, then write down three things that are already enough.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#clarity #marcusaurelius #stoicism #gratitude #mindset

text: “Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.”
He wrote this as a Roman emperor, for his own eyes only.
Even with an empire, he reminded himself of the basics.
We keep adding to the list of what we need.
A better phone. A better title. A better week.
Marcus points somewhere smaller.
The way you think about what you already have.
That is not a trick to ignore real problems.
It is a way to stop adding imaginary ones.
Try this tonight:
Write down three things that are already enough.
Read them out loud once.
Clarity often starts with subtraction.
Less wanting. More noticing.
What do you already have that you keep forgetting to notice?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
Small daily practices that make things clearer.
Notice what is enough.
*Clarity follows.*

caption:
Your world is only as wide as what you can see.

Save this for the next time you feel certain.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#innerspeech #schopenhauer #perspective #selftalk #mindset

text: “Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world.”
Schopenhauer wrote this in the 1850s.
It still describes most arguments we have.
What you cannot see feels like it does not exist.
That is how a small view becomes a whole world.
Your inner voice has a field of vision too.
It speaks from what you already know.
That is why the same thought repeats.
It has nowhere new to look.
Try this:
Ask someone who disagrees with you what they see.
Do not argue. Just listen to the view.
You are not looking for a new opinion.
You are widening the frame.
What might you be missing because it sits outside your view?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
A wider view starts with a quieter, curious voice.
Widen the frame.
*Hear a new voice.*
